blocks.text: IT and digital services companies receive a steady flow of project inquiries. Most arrive as short, informal messages, such as "I need an e-commerce website for my clothing business." Before a sales or project team can respond usefully, someone must work out which service is needed, collect missing requirements, judge how serious the inquiry is, record the details, and follow up. This work is repetitive and easy to delay.

This document proposes an AI Lead Qualification & Project Requirement Automation for Star Developer, the sample IT and digital services business selected for this exercise. The proposed solution reads each inquiry, identifies the requested service, extracts the available details, asks for what is missing, classifies the inquiry, prepares a structured lead record, and notifies the right team. People remain responsible for pricing, negotiation, and every complex or sensitive decision.

blocks.title: Selected problem
blocks.text: AI-Powered Lead Qualification & Project Requirement Collection.

An initial inquiry such as "I need an e-commerce website for my clothing business" tells the team what the customer wants, but not the details needed to plan the work: the number of products, payment methods, delivery needs, existing domain or hosting, and extra features. Collecting these details by hand for every inquiry is repetitive, and the cost grows with the number of inquiries.

blocks.title: Scenario, Not a Verified Fact
blocks.text: The problem is presented as a realistic business-process scenario for designing a solution. It is not a claim that Star Developer currently faces these problems or has any existing automation.

Customer messages are written in natural language, and every customer words things differently. Fixed-rule automation struggles with this. AI can read varied messages, identify the service, extract details, and write suitable follow-up questions, which makes it a strong fit for this process.

rows: The customer sends a project inquiry.

The human team follows up with an organized, better-qualified potential customer.

Why would a business pay for this automation? From a business owner's point of view, the value is in making the first stage of every project inquiry faster, more consistent, and less dependent on staff availability:
Time saved and productivity: staff stop typing the same clarifying questions and spend more time on project discussions.
Faster lead handling: inquiries are acknowledged and organized right away.
Better organization and less repetitive work: every lead is stored with the same fields, and data entry and forwarding are handled by the workflow.
Improved customer experience: customers receive clear, relevant questions instead of waiting.
Consistent processing and better follow-up: every inquiry follows the same rules, and qualified leads reach the team with context.

blocks.text: End-to-End Solution Summary
Result: an organized lead, a faster response, and a better business process.

This document identified a realistic business-process problem for an IT and digital services company: handling early- stage project inquiries by hand. It analyzed the manual process, explained why it suits automation, and designed a practical solution that reads inquiries, collects missing requirements, qualifies leads, prepares structured records, and notifies the team.

The design is realistic because it keeps people in charge of pricing, contracts, negotiation, and sensitive cases, and because it recommends tools and an implementation roadmap without claiming that anything has been built. The value comes from solving a genuine business problem with a clear workflow, not from using AI for its own sake.

AI suits this process because customer messages are written in varied natural language.
